title: Representable presheaves are sheaves on the small etale site
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $X\to T$ be a $T$-scheme. The presheaf $h_X$ on $T_{\Et}$ defined by $h_X(U)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,X)$ is a sheaf of sets for the etale topology: for every etale covering family $(U_i\to U)_i$, morphisms $U_i\to X$ which agree after pullback to $U_i\times_UU_j$ glue uniquely to a morphism $U\to X.

proof.text: Let (U_i → U) be an etale covering family in T_Et. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] it is an fpqc covering of U. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with base U and target X to the compatible scheme morphisms U_i → X: compatibility means equality after composition with the two projections of U_i ×_U U_j. This yields a unique scheme morphism g:U → X restricting to the given maps. Write p:X → T and u:U → T for the structure maps. The composites p ∘ g and u restrict to the same maps U_i → T because every given map is a T-morphism. Apply the uniqueness clause of the same descent node again, with target T, to conclude p ∘ g = u. Thus g is a T-morphism. Absolute uniqueness also gives uniqueness among T-morphisms; this is precisely the sheaf equalizer condition.
